question: What does RevFactor actually do — is it just pricing?
answer: We're a full revenue management service, not just a dynamic-pricing toggle. We optimize the listing's SEO/positioning, run comp and market analysis, build a full-year pricing strategy, then adjust it daily — promotions, discounts, gap-filling, and repositioning based on how the property paces vs. the market. Frame it as 'we turn the property into a cash machine' and own the entire revenue function so the owner doesn't.

question: How is this different from me just running Price Labs myself?
answer: Price Labs is one tool inside revenue management, not the whole thing — it's 'a Ferrari being driven to the grocery store.' It only reads location/beds/baths/guests and needs a human-set base price; it doesn't see amenities, reviews, new-listing boost, or timing. We use Price Labs plus pacing analysis, manual strategy, OTA markups/discounts, and Rankbreeze data, and we do it daily. Self-managing hosts simply don't have the time or tooling to dig in every day.

question: What is 'pacing' and why does it justify the service?
answer: Pacing is our edge: for any future period (e.g., July) we compare how booked you are today vs. the same point last year and vs. the live market. If you're booked faster than the market you're underpriced (raise); if you're pacing behind, you're overpriced (adjust or discount). Booking window is a median, not a deadline — we read it alongside occupancy. This is what separates real revenue management from random price-dropping.

question: Do you optimize the listing / SEO / photos, or only price?
answer: We review the listing on onboarding and share optimization suggestions — photo tour setup, captions, clean titles (no all-caps, asterisks, emojis), amenity ordering, descriptions. We use Rankbreeze to see where in the funnel guests drop (not showing on page 1 vs. clicking but not booking) and recommend fixes. Be honest: copy tweaks 'don't move the needle as much' as pricing, but we do flag and suggest changes. The owner makes the edits.

question: What does it cost?
answer: Flat $350/month per listing, a one-time $150 onboarding fee (per account, not per listing), and $50/month for each child (sub-)listing. Keep it simple — flat fee, no percentage of revenue.

question: Why a flat fee instead of a percentage like a property manager?
answer: Flat fee keeps it simple and is a no-brainer that pays for itself — usually just one extra night or a little ADR covers it, and everything above that is the owner's. Position it against the typical 15-20% PM cut: revenue management alone shouldn't cost a fifth of their revenue. Our incentive isn't a commission — it's our reputation, since the whole business runs on referrals and word of mouth.

question: How do child / sub-listings get priced?
answer: When one property is split into multiple listings (e.g., a parent six-bedroom plus a smaller three-bedroom 'child,' or a duplex listed as Unit A, Unit B, and combined), the main listing is the full $350/month and each additional child listing is $50/month. Example: one property listed three ways = $350 + $50 + $50. At signup they pick the number of properties and add the child-listing add-ons.

question: What software costs does the owner save?
answer: They stop paying for Price Labs (we host their listing under our account) and they get Rankbreeze included — together roughly $50/month in software they'd otherwise pay for. Use this to show the net cost is lower than the sticker price.

question: Can you guarantee you'll increase my revenue? What if results are flat?
answer: Don't promise a number. Lean on the three-month commitment that's then month-to-month: it gives us time to master the property and prove value, and if it's not working they can cancel after three months with 30 days' notice. Reinforce with case studies and testimonials from well-known hosts. Typical lift is ~20-35%, often even with the market declining — but stay honest that it depends on property, market, and reviews.

question: I want to be involved / review pricing weekly (e.g., for tax material participation).
answer: Set the expectation firmly but kindly: we do NOT do strategy calls or weekly price reviews — it's not scalable at this price and we change prices daily. We sell an outcome, not education, and the strategy is our proprietary IP. Many clients still get tax benefits (they track participation their own way), but we can't run every price change past the owner. If they push hard on micromanagement, that's a yellow flag — we recently dropped a client over exactly that.

question: My market is too saturated / it's a slow year / I can't reinvest in the property.
answer: Acknowledge it — supply is up and demand is flat in many markets, which is exactly why pricing strategy matters most now. Our case studies outperformed last year even while their markets declined. We work with what they have (no required capital reinvestment): separate child listings, length-of-stay strategy, and gap-filling can lift revenue without a renovation.

question: Will a co-host on my account hurt my guest experience or branding?
answer: No. The co-host is a clean account (partner Gaston's name/photo, no reviews, no branding) used only to edit the calendar and access Airbnb's custom pricing tools. We never message guests or touch communications. It only shows if a guest scrolls to the bottom of the listing, and across 60+ clients it's never caused an issue.

question: My listing already prices above all the comps — is it worth it for you to take?
answer: Be consultative, not pushy. Offer to run a report if they send the exact address plus a revenue/occupancy export, and tell them honestly if there's little room. It's fine to suggest they start with only their lower-performing or higher-revenue property and treat it as an A/B test — that builds trust and usually leads to the rest of the portfolio (mirror the Smokies client who handed over all 30 after three months).

question: How do I explain the parent/child listing strategy for large properties?
answer: For big homes that are hard to fill midweek or off-season (you can't book 20+ people last-minute), we create a second smaller listing of the same house — e.g., a 6-bed listed as a 3-bed — negotiate a lower cleaning fee, and rent it to smaller groups. Guests are told they may use only the booked rooms or pay the full rate; in practice it's rarely an issue. This captures demand that would otherwise sit vacant and can be the difference in hitting annual revenue goals.

question: Why not just add an extra-guest fee instead of a child listing?
answer: Extra-guest fees above a threshold distort high-season pricing — if you optimize the per-guest fee for slow midweeks, you throw off your peak pricing for max occupancy. A separate child listing lets us target smaller groups in dead periods without compromising the full-property high-season rate. It's a cleaner way to price for two very different buyers.

question: How fast will the owner see results?
answer: Small results almost immediately — we apply proven rules (OTA markups with baked-in discounts) on day one, so bookings can start within days, especially on open calendars or new listings. Bigger lift builds over a week or two and depends on how much future availability exists. Set the expectation that pricing is a moving target we keep adjusting.

question: What proof points / case studies should I cite?
answer: Use the real examples: Minneapolis (+~$10k in one quarter), Hillsdale/Hudson Valley NY (+$12.4k Q4), Bourbon Trail KY (+$6.6k Q4 — emphasize the large % increase on a smaller property), and the Smokies luxury-cabin owner who split 30 cabins between us and a competitor and gave us all of them after three months. Stress that many of these gains came while the broader market was declining. Offer the testimonial video from recognizable hosts in the space.

question: What access and tools do you need to start?
answer: Add our co-host account on Airbnb (calendar only), add us as a user on their PMS (Hospitable, Guesty, Hostaway, etc.), and transfer their Price Labs listing to us via a quick email to Price Labs support (keeps all history; reversible). If they use Beyond Pricing they can cancel it. We also fill out a Property Discovery intake form. No PMS or Price Labs of their own is required — we set it up.

question: Why do you mark up rates and then add discounts? Won't owners think it's odd?
answer: Explain the psychology: Airbnb rewards and showcases listings that use its discount tools (early bird, last-minute, length-of-stay) and guests love the strike-through 'deal.' So we mark the rate up ~40% in Price Labs, push it to the OTAs, then bake in discounts there — never discount in Price Labs, because the guest must see the strike-through on Airbnb/VRBO. The discounted price IS our target price; it just ranks better and converts more. Pre-empt the 'why am I discounting in summer?' question.

question: How long does onboarding take and what's the timeline to go live?
answer: About 2-3 business days (48 hours, sometimes up to 5) once we have the intake form and access; Price Labs usually transfers the listing within 24 hours. We start tweaking on day one and keep refining the first few weeks. For pre-launch owners, they can sign up once the listing is built (photos ready) — we can pause billing until they go live, and we price BEFORE launch, not after.

question: Can you work with owners who still have a property manager?
answer: We prefer self-managing owners, but we can work with a PM if we manage the whole portfolio's revenue. The catch: we must protect our proprietary strategy — a PM with access could see our markup/discount rule system and replicate it across other properties. So handle with care, and clarify the PM hands over only the revenue piece. Note onboarding requests for the chat-based support model so PMs don't expect calls either.
